source.title: Incorruptible Neural Networks: Training Models that can Generalize to Large Internal Perturbations
source.authors: P. Jacobson; Ben Feinberg; Suhas Kumar; S. Agarwal; T. Xiao; C. Bennett

record.file_problem: None; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests how training perturbations and measured sharpness relate to generalization under internal weight noise, an extension beyond the listed versions' natural-label generalization settings.
record.gate_note: The paper reports noisy train and test accuracy for RWP, SAM, schedules, and simulated hardware, and measures gradient norms and sharpness. Its focus is noise-robust generalization under internal weight perturbations, not the natural-label generalization gap described in most versions.
record.test_reason: The study measures robustness to internal weight noise and compares perturbative training methods. It does not test V7's relationship between magnitude-aware training-error sharpness and the ordinary train–test error gap among similarly well-fitted networks. Training-versus-test loss sharpness is a different relationship. None of V1–V6 or V8 is tested either.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially accurate. The authors argue that over-regularized RWP improves noise-robust generalization, SAM is superior for small noise but encounters optimization difficulties at large perturbations, and dynamic perturbation schedules mitigate those difficulties. They attribute the optimization difficulties to flatness-induced vanishing gradients and validate the practical trends with analog-hardware simulations.
record.recipe_differences: Studies robustness to internal weight noise using SAM and random-weight perturbation, rather than the natural-label generalization interventions in the listed versions.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcome depends on training perturbation method and strength, test-noise strength, perturbation schedule, backbone, and simulated hardware noise profile.

fits_no_version.finding: Stronger-than-test RWP noise can improve noisy held-out accuracy despite worse noisy training accuracy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Training with weight noise stronger than deployment noise can improve generalization under internal weight perturbations.

fits_no_version.finding: SAM performs better at small test-noise strengths, while RWP performs better at larger strengths; large fixed SAM perturbations can impede optimization.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The relative noise robustness of SAM and RWP depends on perturbation strength and optimization stability.

fits_no_version.finding: Training and test loss sharpness can become anti-correlated during optimization, and flatter training landscapes need not yield flatter test landscapes.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Training-loss flatness alone need not predict test-loss flatness or internal-noise robustness along SAM/RWP training trajectories.

fits_no_version.finding: Tuned perturbation ramps improve noisy test accuracy, and the preferred training method varies between simulated RRAM and SONOS hardware.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Perturbation schedules and hardware noise profiles affect the accuracy of models deployed with internal weight noise.

record.problems: The paper studies noise-robust generalization rather than the natural-label generalization gap in the claim. Main results use ResNet-18; other backbones and datasets appear in appendices. Reported uncertainties reflect noise samples and three trained weight sets.
record.rows_left_out: The paper reports additional condition-specific results in Tables 1–4, 6–12 and Figures 1–16. These are not all extracted because the 60-row cap is unnecessary for the mapped version: selected rows retain the main train/test gap pattern, sharpness findings, schedule effect, and hardware-dependent comparisons. Other table entries vary σtrain, ρ, test-noise strength, backbone, dataset, schedule, or hardware.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting alongside natural-label held-out performance under the same architecture and training recipe.
Test error as width increases beyond a demonstrated zero-training-error threshold. Table 8 varies width but does not establish interpolation or comparable zero-error fits.
Convolutional versus fully connected classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning. SAM and RWP use SGD as their base optimizer.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that offset large-batch penalties.
Dropout interventions and removing dropout together with weight decay. Weight decay and augmentation are recipe components here, not controlled interventions.

Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance before training error rises as a predictor of ordinary train–test error gaps among similarly well-fitted networks, including comparison with norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing highly memorized training examples versus removing equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: Remove the record's V7 limits_scope verdict: a different sharpness measure and a noise-robustness outcome do not qualify the stated V7 correlation. Appendix B reports augmentation, weight decay, label smoothing, and selection of checkpoints by highest perturbed test accuracy; the results therefore involve test-based checkpoint selection. The first reported uncertainty is variation across noise samples, and the second is variation across three trained weight sets.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label test performance.
Width sweeps past interpolation on natural labels.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD on the listed benchmarks.
Natural-label gap without internal noise; direct ranking of magnitude-aware sharpness against norm- and margin-based measures; CIFAR-10 and SVHN.

rows.subject: ResNet-18
rows.measure: Noisy train accuracy; noisy test accuracy
rows.uncertainty: Two reported uncertainty values per metric
rows.note: Compared with the matched σtrain = 0.02 setting, the more strongly regularized model has lower noisy training accuracy and higher noisy test accuracy.
rows.check: Numbers match Table 10, but noisy train/test accuracy under different RWP objectives does not establish V7's sharpness–generalization-gap relationship; training accuracies also differ substantially.

rows.subject: ResNet-18
rows.measure: Noisy train accuracy; noisy test accuracy
rows.uncertainty: Two reported uncertainty values per metric
rows.note: Higher training noise corresponds to lower noisy training accuracy and higher noisy test accuracy in this comparison.
rows.check: Baseline is mislabeled: 76.95 training accuracy and 50.68 test accuracy belong to σtrain = 0.06, not 0.05. The σtrain = 0.05 values are 78.81 ± 4.08 ± 2.63 and 48.54 ± 2.18 ± 0.70. Neither comparison measures V7.

rows.subject: ResNet-18
rows.note: The paper reports that for every test-noise setting, best RWP performance uses training noise greater than test noise.
rows.check: Numbers match Table 1. This compares noisy test performance across RWP strengths without measuring a sharpness–gap relationship.

rows.subject: ResNet-18
rows.note: Authors state SAM produces better-generalizing minima than any corresponding RWP or SGD weights for small test noise.
rows.check: The best RWP baseline at σtest = 0.02 is 77.65 ± 0.26 ± 0.05 with σtrain = 0.05, not 77.64 ± 0.25 ± 0.36. SAM accuracy is correct. Optimizer performance alone does not measure V7.

rows.subject: ResNet-18
rows.note: Large fixed SAM perturbation performs much worse at this test-noise level; paper attributes large-perturbation difficulty to vanishing gradients.
rows.check: Numbers match Table 2. Poor performance with large SAM perturbations is an optimization/robustness result, not a reversal of V7's correlation.

rows.subject: ResNet-18
rows.note: Ramped perturbation improves on the constant-perturbation SAM baseline.
rows.check: This is the proposed schedule's performance against constant SAM, not a test of any version. The comparison includes tuning terminal perturbation strength and warmup length; it does not isolate schedule shape at matched terminal strength. It is repeated in R9.

rows.subject: ResNet-18
rows.operation_detail: Tracked average-direction training and test sharpness during optimization
rows.measure: Relationship between training sharpness and test sharpness over training
rows.value: Authors report test sharpness is almost always greater than training sharpness; toward later epochs the two are anti-correlated.
rows.note: The authors also report strong evidence against a direct correlation between training and test sharpness.
rows.check: The stated finding matches Appendix D.5, which also examines σ = 0.02 in Figure 10. It concerns training-loss sharpness versus test-loss sharpness over optimization, not magnitude-aware training-error sharpness versus the ordinary generalization gap among similarly fitted networks.

rows.subject: ResNet-18
rows.operation_detail: Compared gradient sharpness of SAM and RWP trajectories
rows.value: SAM perturbations encounter sharper gradient sharpness than large RWP perturbations at every point in the loss landscape.
rows.note: The paper links this to smaller SAM gradients and optimization stagnation at large perturbations.
rows.check: Section 5.2 compares ascent-direction sharpness for SAM with average-direction sharpness for RWP along sampled training trajectories. This is an optimization diagnostic, not V7's measure or outcome. The row overstates the scope by saying every point in the loss landscape.

rows.subject: ResNet-18
rows.operation_detail: SAM and RWP with quadratic perturbation schedules
rows.uncertainty: Two reported uncertainty values per metric
rows.note: Both scheduled methods improve test accuracy over their constant-perturbation counterparts.
rows.check: These are proposed-method comparisons rather than evidence for a claim version; the SAM comparison duplicates R6. Values match Table 3, but Table 12 reports 65.57 ± 2.05 ± 0.64 for the selected quadratic RWP configuration, inconsistent with Table 3's 65.27.

rows.subject: ResNet-18
rows.uncertainty: Two reported uncertainty values per metric
rows.note: The paper reports RWP outperforming SAM on the larger-noise RRAM simulation, with a further gain from the schedule.
rows.check: Numbers match Table 5. Simulated hardware inference accuracy compares noise-robust training methods and does not measure V7's sharpness–gap relationship.

rows.subject: ResNet-18
rows.uncertainty: Two reported uncertainty values per metric
rows.note: For small-noise SONOS, SAM exceeds RWP; the SAM schedule further improves accuracy.
rows.check: Numbers match Table 5. This is a simulated hardware performance comparison, not partial evidence for V7. In this condition RWP σ = 0.05 performs below SGD.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Internal weight noise on the tested image datasets and ResNet-family models
reader_labels.reason: Noise-robust test performance varies with perturbation method and strength, and training sharpness does not directly track test sharpness; see R1–R9.
